title: The Imperfect Tense (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Marfūʿ)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 14; Ryding Ch. 21 §21.1, Ch. 34)
objectives: Recognize the four imperfect prefixes (أَ, تَـ, يَـ, نَـ) and person/number suffixes.
Identify indicative mood markers (ḍammah on singulars, retained nūn on al-afʿāl al-khamsah).
Negate imperfect verbs with لَا and express future tense with سَـ and سَوْفَ.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 12: What suffixes mark the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd person in the past tense (al-māḍī)?

sections.heading: Imperfect Prefixes & Indicative Mood
sections.body: The imperfect (al-muḍāriʿ) expresses ongoing, habitual, or future actions. Unlike the past tense (which uses suffixes only), the imperfect uses a prefix from أَنَيْتُ (أَ 'I', تَـ 'you/she', يَـ 'he/they', نَـ 'we') plus suffixes for dual, plural, and 2nd-person feminine singular.

sections.label: Indicative Mood Markers (Al-Rafʿ)
sections.summary: With no governing particle preceding it, the imperfect is indicative (marfūʿ): sound singulars end in ḍammah (-u), while the five dual/plural forms (al-afʿāl al-khamsah: يَفْعَلَانِ, تَفْعَلَانِ, يَفْعَلُونَ, تَفْعَلُونَ, تَفْعَلِينَ) retain their final nūn.

sections.heading: Form I Imperfect Indicative (يَكْتُبُ — he writes)

sections.translation: The student will write the lesson.
sections.irab: سَـ: حَرْفُ اسْتِقْبَالٍ | يَكْتُبُ: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِالضَّمَّةِ | الطَّالِبُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ
sections.notes: Future particles سَـ (near future) and سَوْفَ do not alter the indicative mood of the verb.

sections.heading: Negating Past vs. Present
sections.body: Use مَا before a past-tense verb (مَا كَتَبَ 'he did not write') and لَا before an imperfect indicative verb (لَا يَكْتُبُ 'he does not write').
